title: Proactive microbatch watermarking and admission-control for KV-cache-aware GPU pressure
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS spikes our continuous-batching pipeline occasionally produces microbatches that push GPU resident KV cache and model activations past safe headroom. This causes KV-eviction churn, increased p95 latency, and degraded throughput. Current heuristics react after eviction or OOM signals which is too late for predictable SLOs.

Goal: Implement a proactive watermarking + admission-control layer that uses lightweight GPU memory pressure signals and KV-cache occupancy to limit microbatch admission (or switch to lower-memory model variants) before hard eviction occurs. This should reduce tail latency and eviction rate while preserving throughput as much as possible.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Deploy canary with 5% traffic for 72h with new admission-control enabled.
2) Eviction-triggered model reloads should drop by >= 70% versus baseline during the same traffic pattern.
3) p95 latency for short sequences (<256 tokens) should not increase by more than 10% and p99 should improve by >= 10%.
4) KV hit ratio should remain within 3 percentage points of baseline or improve.
5) New metrics (watermarked_batches, admission_rate, early_fallbacks) are emitted and dashboards exist.
6) No customer-facing rate-limit regressions for P0 customers in Dedicated fleets during rollout.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Maintain two memory watermarks per GPU: soft_watermark (e.g., 70% of usable GPU memory) and hard_watermark (e.g., 92%).
- Track KV-cache occupancy (bytes and shard-level occupancy) and estimated activation headroom per model variant.
- Implement an admission controller upstream of microbatch formation that consults a pressure scoreboard (recent GPU memory usage, KV eviction_rate, inflight_batches).
- If scoreboard >= soft_watermark, admission controller will: (a) prioritize merging to existing microbatches for compatible requests; (b) lower batch_size_target for new microbatches; (c) route compatible requests to low-memory quantized model variant or CPU fallback if configured.
- If scoreboard >= hard_watermark, admission controller will refuse new microbatches (throttle) and trigger fallback policy (route to region with headroom or queue with backoff).
- Add reservoir tokens per worker to avoid synchronized admission storms; tokens replenished proportional to measured throughput and KV hit trend.
- Use exponential smoothing window (configurable) for scoreboard to prevent oscillation on short spikes.
- Integrate with existing KV eviction heuristics: when admission controller reduces admission, lower eviction aggressiveness to avoid evicting useful KV entries prematurely.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive early throttling reduces tail but increases apparent rejection which may affect client retries. We prefer graceful degradation (route to smaller model) over hard drops for PLG customers.
- Precise per-request activation cost prediction is expensive; we use inexpensive heuristics (sequence length bucket, model variant profile, recent prefix cache hit rates) with periodic calibration from sampled traces.

Performance testing notes: use synthetic spike generator (existing bench tool) with mixed sequence-length distributions and 10-1000 qps per worker to measure behavior. Collect trace samples to validate activation estimator accuracy.
rollout_plan:
1) Unit tests + integration tests in CI (runtime/pipeline).
2) Internal canary on staging with scripted spike generator for 48h.
3) Canary deploy to production with 5% traffic and observability alert thresholds.
4) If canary metrics meet acceptance criteria, ramp to 25% for 24h, then 100% over 48h.
5) For Dedicated fleets, ship as opt-in config flag; default off for customers with custom capacity contracts until we validate.

Rollback criteria: sustained p95 increase > 20% or unexpected OOMs/evictions > baseline by 15% for 15m.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Metrics to emit: watermarked_batches (counts by worker/model/variant), admission_rate, token_reservoir_level, early_fallback_count, kv_eviction_rate, gpu_mem_headroom, activation_estimate_error_percent.
Alerts: high eviction_rate (>= baseline+15%), reservoir starvation for > 5m, admission_rate drop > 50% on healthy traffic. Dashboards: per-region scoreboard heatmap, per-variant fallbacks, and SLO overlays.
Logging: sample per-request admission decision (sample rate 0.1%) with reason code for offline analysis.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overly conservative watermarks reduce throughput for users. Mitigation: start with high soft_watermark and tighten in stages; provide customer override and opt-in.
Risk: Admission coordination across workers adds latency. Mitigation: use local per-worker scoreboard with occasional cross-worker reconciliation; keep decision in fast path.
Risk: Fallback to quantized variant may change model output quality. Mitigation: tie to quality-monitoring and only enable for tolerant routes; add A/B evals for customers.
